status: Exploratory reanalysis of already viewed clinical outcomes; protocol fixed before this paired-comparison calculation, not a new outcome-blind study.
decision: Does treatment-aligned signal construction provide a positive coverage gain versus a training-selected single-component baseline under the same 10% expected overall wrong-release-risk procedure?

primary.split: Reuse original F78 hash-ranked 42 training / 42 calibration / 43 test split, seed release-calibration-v2-20261001; never reshuffle.
primary.population: Test patients whose clinical treatment string includes radiation, capecitabine and irinotecan. Population membership selected from treatment fields before paired-result calculation. 5-FU remains the assay proxy for capecitabine.
primary.fit_population: Same existing 42 training and 42 calibration patients for both signals; restrict primary evaluation by regimen only, so the original full-population risk guarantee does not automatically transfer to the subgroup.
primary.new_signal: Measured combined irradiation + 5-FU + irinotecan assay (one readout).
primary.single_baseline: Choose among irradiation, 5-FU and irinotecan using training balanced accuracy with each cutoff fitted only to those 42 patients; ties favor original channel order. This is training-best single-component, not test oracle.
primary.margins: Identical fixed GRID [-1] + [0,0.01,...,1] and training-only reference ECDF; separate calibration per signal using same expected overall-risk CRC selection.
primary.conditional: Report each identical fixed-sequence conditional LTT result separately; alpha=.1 and one-source eta=.05.
primary.outcome: TRG 0/1 or cCR/pCR positive, other TRG negative.

sensitivity: All 43 original rectal test patients with unchanged models and certificates.

Tiriac primary 7 and stricter 6 use unchanged frozen mean-rank and fixed-anchor predictions. No labelled training/calibration cohort exists for Tiriac; fixed-anchor is not asserted to be the best single drug. Tiriac supplies observed equal-coverage accuracy evidence, not a 10% risk certificate.
Original rectal two-readout agreement comparator retained only under that exact name; it is not a single-drug baseline.

statistics.method: paired percentile bootstrap; within-source resampling for cross-source descriptive aggregate, preserving source sample sizes; 2.5/97.5 percentiles
statistics.primary_effect: CRC new coverage minus training-best single-component CRC coverage
statistics.error_effect: At fixed full coverage, comparator wrong-call fraction minus new-signal wrong-call fraction
statistics.paired_tests: Two-sided exact McNemar binomial test for discordant patient-level release indicators and separately for full-coverage correctness; cross-source test sums discordances as a descriptive shared directional null, never pools endpoint/risk calibration.
statistics.gate: Both methods observed overall wrong-release risk <=10%, and paired 95% coverage-gain interval lower bound >0. Subgroup label limits population-risk interpretation.

cross_source: Rectal matched subgroup plus Tiriac primary seven: source-stratified descriptive error reduction at full coverage; endpoints remain distinct and no cross-source exchangeability or pooled risk guarantee is claimed.
constraints: No paid calls; one single-thread low-priority process; first 100 bootstrap replicates measure RSS, final 10000 run only within 4 GB and 5 minutes.
